pattern_id: Crash-window safety-rules rollback enables double-vote and conflicting QCs
description: In Aptos SafetyRules, the persistent SafetyData (last_voted_round, preferred_round, last_vote, etc.) is not atomically coupled to vote emission. If a node crashes after returning a signed vote but before durably persisting the updated SafetyData, on restart SafetyRules can be reinitialized from stale SafetyData that predates the vote. Under this stale state, construct_and_sign_vote_two_chain will accept a second proposal in the same (epoch, round) and produce a second vote with the same author but a different block id. An adversary that observes both votes can combine them with votes from other validators to form two conflicting Quorum Certificates (QCs) for different blocks in the same (epoch, round) using only f designated Byzantine validators in a 3f+1 system. These conflicting QCs can drive executions that double-commit distinct blocks at the same height for different honest validators, violating safety and agreement.
trigger_condition: 1) SafetyRules stores its SafetyData in a persistent backend but does not durably update it before (or atomically with) emitting a vote; 2) A validator H signs a vote in round r and sends it, but the process crashes before persisting SafetyData with last_voted_round >= r and last_vote = that vote; 3) On restart, SafetyRules is re-created from the stale SafetyData (last_voted_round < r, last_vote = None); 4) A conflicting proposal for the same (epoch, round r) is presented to SafetyRules; 5) construct_and_sign_vote_two_chain is called again for this conflicting proposal and returns a second vote instead of an error or replay of the original vote.
test_template: 1) Instantiate a validator signer H and construct an EpochState and genesis QC via existing test helpers (e.g., make_genesis). 2) Manually create pre-crash SafetyData with last_voted_round = r-1 and last_vote = None, and initialize a SafetyRules instance over an in-memory PersistentSafetyStorage with that SafetyData. 3) Build a proposal A at (epoch e, round r) extending the genesis QC and call construct_and_sign_vote_two_chain; assert this first vote succeeds and record its vote_data().proposed().id() as block_id(A). 4) Simulate a crash-window rollback by dropping the SafetyRules instance and reinitializing a new SafetyRules over a fresh PersistentSafetyStorage seeded with the same stale SafetyData (last_voted_round = r-1, last_vote = None), without injecting any knowledge of the previous vote. 5) Build a conflicting proposal A' at the same (epoch e, round r) and same parent QC but with a different payload so it has a different block id; call construct_and_sign_vote_two_chain again. 6) Assertion 1: If the second call returns Ok(vote'), assert that vote'.vote_data().proposed().id() != block_id(A); this shows per-validator double-voting for (e, r). 7) Assertion 2: Construct two QCs QC1 and QC2 for blocks A and A' respectively using 2f+1 signatures from a 3f+1 validator set where only f validators are designated Byzantine, and verify that both QCs pass quorum_cert::QuorumCert::verify under a common ValidatorVerifier; this demonstrates that conflicting QCs can be formed with only f Byzantine validators. 8) (Optional) Integrate SafetyRules into a RoundManager + NetworkPlayground environment to drive a full BFT execution in which different honest nodes commit A and A' at the same height, showing a double-commit in practice.
